An AND list has the form command1 && command2 command2 is executed if, and only if, command1 returns an exit status of zero (success). An OR list has the form command1 || command2 command2 is executed if, and only if, command1 returns a non-zero exit status. decisions.support_rationale: The whole original paragraph overstates the protection supplied by sshd -t and excludes documented SIGHUP reload. The complete replacement retains the useful conditional restart explanation, states the actual syntax/key check, and removes the outage guarantee.
decisions.method_rationale: Primary OpenSSH, shell and service-manager definitions support the corrected instruction. No runtime login or restart success is claimed or required to establish these source semantics.
decisions.limitation: No daemon reload/restart, lockout or continuity was tested. The existing separate key-only login and recovery instructions remain necessary operational guidance.
decisions.next_action: Apply the exact whole-paragraph replacement only in the separately authorized follow-up; retain the original assertion/history and run the existing targeted projection/anchor checks.
decisions.replacement_text:
`sshd -t` checks configuration validity and key sanity. The `&&` runs the
restart only after that check succeeds; it cannot guarantee a successful
restart or continued access. Configuration edits affect the daemon after it
reloads or restarts.

decisions.support_rationale: The original compound equates a configuration value with completed verification and promises error clearing in about two hours without a bound product source. The replacement instead requires the already documented separate key-only connection check and recommends reassessing the warning and contacting support if it persists. It makes no timing, successful-login or backend-clearing assertion.
decisions.method_rationale: The retained OpenSSH client source defines publickey authentication selection, while the complete adjacent page instructions establish the existing separate-connection verification and retained original session. Rechecking an unresolved status and contacting support with facts is proportionate advice, not a product guarantee needing new hardware tests.
decisions.limitation: No login, warning clearance or elapsed-time behavior was observed. Removing the unsupported promise does not verify the old two-hour policy assertion; that exact owner question remains separately recorded below and in the original proposal/history.
decisions.next_action: Apply this complete replacement in the separate adjacent follow-up, preserve the original assertion and its unresolved owner question, and retain existing procedure/runtime status. No claimed temporal guarantee remains in the replacement.
decisions.replacement_text:
After applying the changes, confirm that a separate key-only SSH connection
works before closing the original session. Recheck the machine’s status; if
the password-login warning persists, contact support with the current warning
and the relevant configuration checks.

retained_owner_questions.title: Vast SSH warning clearing trigger and timing
retained_owner_questions.question: What product/verification rule triggers clearing of a password-login machine warning, what cadence/conditions apply, and is approximately two hours an approved expectation?
retained_owner_questions.disposition: The unsupported statement is proposed for removal from customer guidance. Source review of its replacement is not backend validation or an answer to this owner question.
